cards.explanation: The answer is Continually. The LORD tells Moses the oil is "…to keep the lamps burning continually." (Leviticus 24:2). No off switch, no break, friends. I once spent years in the dark, so a light that never goes out sounds like a dream to me.

The answer is evening. Aaron tends the lamps "…from evening until morning." (Leviticus 24:3). That's the night shift, friends, and I have respect for anybody who works it. I'd need a very big timer and a lot of coffee.

The answer is True. The LORD calls it "…a permanent statute for the generations to come." (Leviticus 24:3). So this job isn't just for Aaron's one season. It's meant to carry on down the line. My own edges wore soft over the years, so "permanent" is a big word to me.

The answer is on the gold table before the LORD. The loaves are set "…on the table of pure gold before the LORD." (Leviticus 24:6). A gold table for bread, bakers! I've never had a counter that nice, and I've baked on a few. Mine had a wobbly leg and a mystery stain.

The answer is every Sabbath day. "Every Sabbath day the bread is to be set out before the LORD…" (Leviticus 24:8). Week after week, the same day, the bread goes out. No snooze button, no "I'll do it tomorrow." I once had a whole drawer's worth of free time and still couldn't keep a schedule like that.

The answer is Israelites. The bread is set out "…on behalf of the Israelites as a permanent covenant." (Leviticus 24:8). So the bread stands there for them, week after week. And the word "permanent" shows up again, friends, so that's twice in one passage.

The answer is Aaron and his sons. The bread "…belongs to Aaron and his sons, who are to eat it in a holy place…" (Leviticus 24:9). So it's their portion. Aaron's family gets to eat the bread from the gold table. I'd say that's a pretty great perk.

The answer is False. Aaron and his sons "…are to eat it in a holy place…" (Leviticus 24:9). So the verse doesn't say "anywhere they like." It names a holy place. The text calls the bread "…a most holy part of the food offerings to the LORD…" and I think that's why the place matters.
